extracted.intended_audience: corporate IP teams, patent counsel, IP analysts, R&D managers interested in patent litigation trends
extracted.subtask_description: A summary and analysis of 2024 patent litigation activity across companies, NPEs, technology domains, and a notable legal change affecting design patents. Useful for IP strategy and monitoring litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent subject matter (what design patents protect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patents safeguard a product's visual appearance — shape, pattern, or overall look — as distinct from utility patents, which protect how a product works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use design patents to protect ornamental aspects of products (appearance, pattern, shape). Recognize the difference from utility patents when crafting IP portfolios or challenging/defending rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent obviousness standard (Rosen‑Durling vs Graham factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit in LKQ Corp. v. GM adopted Graham factors to evaluate obviousness of design patents, replacing the previously more rigid Rosen‑Durling test that required a nearly identical prior design to invalidate a design patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication: courts now apply the more flexible Graham utility‑patent obviousness framework to design patents, making it easier to challenge design patents for obviousness. Expect increased design‑patent litigation (noted as a likely trend for 2025), especially in appearance‑sensitive industries (consumer goods, electronics). Example: LKQ v. GM overturned USPTO's Rosen‑Durling‑based rejection of a challenge to GM's fender design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation frequency/counts as a metric of risk/activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of lawsuits and affected patents is used to identify most‑sued companies and most‑litigated patents (e.g., Samsung: 69 lawsuits involving 208 patents; Torus Ventures' US7203844B1 cited in 63 cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative metrics (number of suits, cases per patent, number of patents-involved) are useful indicators for gauging litigation activity and identifying high‑risk targets or hotspots. The article's rankings are based on litigation data through 6 Dec 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Practicing Entity (NPE) behavior and risk profile
rubrics_metrics.description: NPEs do not make products or offer services but monetize patents by licensing or suing; some NPEs file very large numbers of suits (e.g., Patent Armory Inc. filed 123 cases in 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat NPEs as persistent litigation risk: they may 'weaponize' certain patents repeatedly. Defensive strategies (e.g., FTO searches, invalidity contentions, licensing, settlements) should account for active NPEs and commonly asserted patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic drug (ANDA) litigation dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: A surge in ANDA disputes occurs after expiration of patents on high‑revenue drugs as generic companies file ANDAs to enter market; such filings often trigger patent litigation and may lead to confidential settlements that set permitted entry dates contingent on FDA approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In pharmaceutical IP strategy, monitor patent expiry schedules and ANDA filings. Settlement terms can include delayed market entry dates tied to regulatory approval and may be subject to FTC/DOJ review. Example: Cipla–Exelixis settlement permitting generic sales from Jan 1, 2031 subject to FDA approval; lawsuits dropped in Delaware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology domain concentration of litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent litigation in 2024 was concentrated in certain domains — notably computer technology — with many of the most‑litigated patents belonging to that domain (e.g., text‑analysis patents, recursive security protocol patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing litigation risk or patent value, consider domain concentration effects: certain technology areas (computer tech, e‑commerce, fintech) saw higher litigation volumes and cross‑industry defendant lists, indicating broad exposure and defensive monitoring priority.
